blocks.x: CIB margins compress while deal complexity grows: origination research, credit memos, trade documentation and risk reporting all consume expensive analyst hours that agentic systems can compress, with the control discipline investment banks cannot compromise. This page is the operating picture: what runs, what strains, and which capabilities move the numbers that decide the margin.

The work concentrates in credit memo production, trade document handling, intraday risk aggregation, with client onboarding (institutional) close behind. Each of these paths produces data faster than decisions, and the gap between the two is where cost and risk accumulate.
the queues and waits that come up first, Corporate & Investment Banking edition:

items: Pitch books, credit memos and research notes re-type data from terminals and filings; quality varies by analyst stamina.
LCs, trade documents and settlement instructions fail on reference mismatches; exception queues run through time zones.
Counterparty, market and collateral views assemble overnight; intraday exposures are estimates.
Deal rooms and research estates hold market-moving data; insider-risk and exfiltration controls are uneven.
Monte Carlo and VaR grids hit compute ceilings on stress days; desks fly blind exactly when it matters.
Booking and risk platforms resist change; product launch becomes a program.
